We've seen some ICS clients label late-evening slots differently across JP/SG/SYD.

Proposed windows (all local times shown for clarity):
- 16:00–16:45 JST / 15:00–15:45 SGT / 17:00–17:45 AEDT (Sydney)
- 20:30–21:10 JST / 19:30–20:10 SGT / 21:30–22:10 AEDT — late slot if you'd prefer after local business hours

Hi Sofia,

Thanks — appreciate the clarity. The 16:00 JST slot looks best for us (the product and infra folks are available). Quick note on the calendar oddity: our admin forwarded an ICS yesterday that showed the event time correctly but the date flipped to 2026-03-30 in Outlook for a few colleagues — they were viewing in the Australia timezone. So yes, we've had the "date moves to next day" surprise before.

Can you confirm the timezone set on the invite (JST +0900)? If the invite is created in UTC or labeled with an ISO date only (20260329), some clients interpret it relative to local midnight which causes the rollover.

Sofia / Marissa — heads-up on staffing. Engineers can do the 16:00 JST slot but only one senior infra engineer at that hour; the alternative late slot (20:30 JST) would require giving up some overlap with our EU team. Also: note that Sydney is still on AEDT (UTC+11) this week — daylight savings doesn't end until early April — so an invite created as UTC+10 will show a one-hour drift for SYD folks.

For safety, we should:
- Create the calendar event explicitly with timezone = Asia/Tokyo (or specify JST +0900)
- Put local times for JP/SG/SYD in the event description so attendees see the mapping
- Add a Zoom link and an explicit ISO timestamp in the body (e.g. 2026-03-29T16:00:00+09:00) so clients parse it correctly

I'll be available to join at 16:00 JST. Marissa can take notes if we need a recording.

Karthik
